label: copy-phase input p echoed from original positions 1-3 (early recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on steps where the fed-back input is the letter p and that p is original token 1, 2 or 3 (recall_idx 2-4), and the step is not the final output. Essentially no activation on p in the original phase, at the delimiter, on p as the first copied token (recall_idx 1), on p fed back late (recall_idx >= 5), or on any other input token. Magnitude is largest when p is original token 1 (recall_idx 2: top examples like a p ... <DEL> a [p]); that bin holds about 55% of the mass. It falls off for later positions, and activations at recall_idx 4 are mostly weak. Output token, prev token and sequence length have little effect.

issues: Small FP pocket: p echoed at recall_idx 4 when L=6 (to_go=1) is active only 65% of the time (2723 predicted on dev), vs about 95% for L>=7. That accounts for most of the roughly 1238 test FPs. Excluding that case raises precision to 0.99 but drops test F1 to 0.958, so the original predicate is better.

Misses (1204 test steps, 0.2% of mass) are almost all p as the first copied token (recall_idx 1) firing at near-zero activation (0.00-0.09 relative). recall_idx==1 & p has precision 0.06, so this is not a real missed class.

Checked claims: activation is 100% copy phase with 0 on the original phase and delimiter. in_tok p carries 100% of the mass. recall_idx 2/3/4 hold 55%/37%/8% of the mass, which matches 'largest at original token 1, weak at recall_idx 4'. to_go==0 has 90 steps and zero mass. Output, previous token and L have flat lifts. The predicate never fires when correct==0, so copy errors cannot be tested. Test P/R/F1 = 0.970/0.970/0.970 and mass recall 0.998 reproduce.
